problems.title: N-th Fibonacci Number

approaches.name: Naive Recursion
approaches.summary: Tree recursion with two recursive branches per call.
approaches.tradeOff: High exponential time due to overlapping subproblems; O(N) call stack space.
approaches.pros: Simple and mathematically direct.
approaches.cons: Severely redundant calculations leading to exponential time and potential TLE for N > 35.

approaches.name: Linear Iteration
approaches.summary: Single loop computing consecutive terms using two rolling variables.
approaches.tradeOff: Optimal O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
approaches.pros: Fast, no recursion stack overhead, minimal memory.
approaches.cons: Requires tracking rolling state variables.

approaches.name: Memoization / DP
approaches.summary: Recursion with cache array/map or tabular array.
approaches.tradeOff: Trades O(N) auxiliary space to achieve linear O(N) time.
approaches.pros: Eliminates duplicate computations.
approaches.cons: Allocates extra memory compared to rolling iteration.

problems.bestTradeoff: Iteration achieves the optimal O(N) time while using only O(1) auxiliary space, avoiding both recursive call stack depth and memoization array allocations.

problems.title: Factorial Calculation

approaches.name: Recursive Approach
approaches.summary: Calls factorial(n-1) down to base case n <= 1.
approaches.tradeOff: Linear time O(N) with O(N) auxiliary call-stack frames.
approaches.pros: Natural recursive definition.
approaches.cons: Call stack frames consume memory and risk StackOverflowError for very large N.

approaches.name: Iterative Approach
approaches.summary: Single loop multiplying numbers from 1 up to N.
approaches.tradeOff: Linear time O(N) with O(1) constant auxiliary space.
approaches.pros: Same time complexity as recursion but zero call stack overhead.
approaches.cons: Requires explicit loop counter.

problems.bestTradeoff: Both approaches have the same O(N) time complexity, but iteration uses less auxiliary memory O(1) because it avoids recursive call stack allocations.

problems.title: Two Sum

approaches.name: Brute Force (Nested Loops)
approaches.summary: Checks every pair of elements with nested loops.
approaches.tradeOff: Quadratic time O(N^2) but O(1) auxiliary space.
approaches.pros: No extra data structures required.
approaches.cons: Slow for large arrays; can cause Time Limit Exceeded (TLE) when N > 10,000.

approaches.name: Hash Table (One-Pass / Two-Pass)
approaches.summary: Stores seen values in a HashMap or HashSet for O(1) complement lookup.
approaches.tradeOff: Trades O(N) auxiliary space to reduce time to O(N).
approaches.pros: Optimal O(N) average time complexity.
approaches.cons: Allocates extra memory for hash entries.

approaches.name: Sort and Two Pointers
approaches.summary: Sorts the array and uses two converging pointers from both ends.
approaches.tradeOff: O(N log N) time bounded by sorting, with O(1) or O(N) space depending on sort algorithm.
approaches.pros: Predictable memory usage without hash collisions.
approaches.cons: Slower than HashMap and modifies original index ordering unless indices are preserved.

problems.bestTradeoff: Using a HashMap provides O(N) time complexity by trading O(N) space for fast lookups. Brute force uses O(1) space but is O(N^2) time, risking TLE on large arrays.

problems.title: Duplicate Detection

approaches.name: Brute Force (Nested Loops)
approaches.summary: Compares every element with every other element.
approaches.tradeOff: O(N^2) time, O(1) space.
approaches.pros: Simple to implement, no extra space.
approaches.cons: Quadratic time complexity, slow for N > 5,000.

approaches.name: HashSet Lookup
approaches.summary: Inserts elements into a HashSet; returns true if add() fails.
approaches.tradeOff: O(N) time with O(N) auxiliary space.
approaches.pros: Linear time, single pass, early exit.
approaches.cons: Requires O(N) memory for the set.

approaches.name: Sorting Based
approaches.summary: Sorts the array and checks adjacent elements.
approaches.tradeOff: O(N log N) time with O(1) auxiliary space (in-place sort).
approaches.pros: Better time than brute force without using a hash table.
approaches.cons: Modifies input array or requires copy.

problems.bestTradeoff: A HashSet achieves O(N) time at the cost of O(N) memory. If memory is severely constrained, in-place sorting achieves O(N log N) with O(1) auxiliary space.

problems.title: Searching in Sorted Array

approaches.name: Linear Search
approaches.summary: Sequentially inspects each element from index 0 to N-1.
approaches.tradeOff: O(N) time, O(1) space.
approaches.pros: Works on both unsorted and sorted arrays.
approaches.cons: Does not exploit the sorted property; scans unnecessary elements.

approaches.name: Iterative Binary Search
approaches.summary: Halves the search range at each iteration using two pointers low and high.
approaches.tradeOff: O(log N) time, O(1) auxiliary space.
approaches.pros: Optimal time and space; no recursion stack overhead.
approaches.cons: Requires sorted input.

approaches.name: Recursive Binary Search
approaches.summary: Divides range recursively with helper(arr, target, low, high).
approaches.tradeOff: O(log N) time, O(log N) auxiliary space for recursive stack.
approaches.pros: Clean divide-and-conquer formulation.
approaches.cons: Uses extra stack memory compared to the iterative version.

problems.bestTradeoff: Iterative binary search is optimal, offering O(log N) time and O(1) auxiliary space. Linear search fails to take advantage of sorted data.

problems.title: Array Sorting

approaches.name: Bubble / Selection Sort
approaches.summary: Nested loops repeatedly swapping adjacent or minimum elements.
approaches.tradeOff: O(N^2) time with O(1) auxiliary space.
approaches.pros: In-place, simple logic.
approaches.cons: Quadratic time complexity, slow for N > 5,000.

approaches.name: Merge Sort
approaches.summary: Recursively splits the array into halves and merges sorted sub-arrays.
approaches.tradeOff: Guaranteed O(N log N) time, requires O(N) auxiliary space for merging.
approaches.pros: Stable sort, guaranteed O(N log N) worst-case time.
approaches.cons: Requires extra array allocation for temporary storage.

approaches.name: Quick Sort / Dual-Pivot (Arrays.sort)
approaches.summary: Partitions array around a pivot in-place.
approaches.tradeOff: O(N log N) average time, O(log N) recursive stack space.
approaches.pros: Fast in practice with high cache locality.
approaches.cons: Worst case O(N^2) without randomized/dual pivot.

problems.bestTradeoff: Merge Sort and Quick Sort provide O(N log N) time, drastically outperforming O(N^2) Bubble Sort on large inputs. Merge Sort trades O(N) space for stability.

problems.title: Palindrome String Verification

approaches.name: String Reversal
approaches.summary: Creates a reversed copy using StringBuilder.reverse() and compares.
approaches.tradeOff: O(N) time with O(N) auxiliary memory for reversed copy.
approaches.pros: Very concise (1-2 lines).
approaches.cons: Allocates unnecessary heap memory for the reversed string.

approaches.name: Two Pointers (In-Place)
approaches.summary: Compares characters from left and right pointers moving inward.
approaches.tradeOff: O(N) time with O(1) constant auxiliary space.
approaches.pros: No extra heap allocations, early exit on first mismatch.
approaches.cons: Slightly more code than reverse().

problems.bestTradeoff: Two Pointers achieves the same O(N) time but uses O(1) auxiliary space, avoiding string duplication in memory.

problems.title: Valid Anagram Verification

approaches.name: Sorting Characters
approaches.summary: Converts both strings to char arrays, sorts them, and checks equality.
approaches.tradeOff: O(N log N) time, O(N) space for char arrays.
approaches.pros: Simple logic using Arrays.equals().
approaches.cons: Sorting takes O(N log N) time, which is slower than linear frequency counting.

approaches.name: Fixed Frequency Array (int[26])
approaches.summary: Counts character frequencies in a fixed-size 26-element array.
approaches.tradeOff: O(N) linear time with O(1) constant auxiliary space (26 ints).
approaches.pros: Single-pass linear time and minimal constant space.
approaches.cons: Assumes standard alphabet (e.g. lowercase English).

approaches.name: HashMap Character Count
approaches.summary: Maps each character to its occurrence count.
approaches.tradeOff: O(N) time with O(K) space where K is unique character count.
approaches.pros: Supports arbitrary Unicode characters.
approaches.cons: Slightly more overhead than primitive fixed array.

problems.bestTradeoff: A fixed frequency array operates in O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space, beating O(N log N) sorting while avoiding the overhead of HashMap boxing.

problems.title: Check Leap Year

approaches.name: Nested Loops (Brute Force)
approaches.summary: Simulates iterations with nested loops.
approaches.tradeOff: Loops add unnecessary O(N^2) complexity for a problem directly solvable with modulo arithmetic.
approaches.pros: None over direct calculation.
approaches.cons: Unnecessary iterations and risks Time Limit Exceeded (TLE).

approaches.name: Iterative Loop
approaches.summary: Iterates year by year or loop count.
approaches.tradeOff: Unnecessary loop iterations for a problem directly solvable in O(1) with remainder conditions.
approaches.pros: None over direct calculation.
approaches.cons: Unnecessary loop overhead.

approaches.name: Direct Modulo Arithmetic
approaches.summary: Direct conditions using the remainder operator (divisible by 4, except century years unless divisible by 400).
approaches.tradeOff: Direct arithmetic conditions using the remainder operator (divisible by 4, except century years unless divisible by 400) achieve O(1) time and O(1) space; the loops can be removed.
approaches.pros: Optimal O(1) time and space, simple boolean logic without loops.
approaches.cons: Requires correct compound condition logic.

problems.bestTradeoff: A leap-year check is solved in O(1) time and O(1) auxiliary space using direct remainder conditions (divisible by 4, except century years unless divisible by 400) without any loops.
